description:
Advances: specled.tag_scanning

TagScanner.process_statement/4 (lib/specled_ex/tag_scanner.ex:255) pattern-matches only @tag, test, and describe nodes; its catch-all silently drops every other AST node — including {:for, _, _}. A test generated by the common ExUnit idiom 'for x <- xs do @tag spec: ...; test ... end' therefore never reaches the tag_map: the tag is not scanned, not even recorded as a dynamic entry. Downstream, tagged_tests stubs covering such ids emit tagged_tests_cover_missing_tag (false positive) and their strength caps at 'claimed', so adopters using the idiom cannot arm missing_tag at :error or strength floors without tripping on tests that exist and are correctly tagged. Demonstrated in Builder (builder-fnl experiment, 2026-08-11): builder.heroku_connect_introspection.workflow_phase_gating had a correct tagged test inside a for-comprehension (test/builder/agent/workflow_phase_test.exs:391-405) and was reported as having no tag carrier; a crude sweep found ~44 for-blocks with spec tags in that one adopter, mostly masked today by duplicate out-of-loop tags. Fix directions: (1) recurse into {:for, _, [..., [do: block]]} bodies in process_statement (the unrolled body contains one @tag + one test — presence is what matters, multiplicity does not); (2) at minimum emit a dynamic_entry instead of dropping, so the blindness is visible. Note prior art: specled_-q59.11 covered list-VALUED tags, a different gap.
